question:
A 61-year-old woman attends a follow-up visit after being hospitalized for diverticulitis, during which
she received intravenous antibiotics and experienced complete symptom resolution. A CT scan
performed during her hospitalization incidentally revealed a 6.2 cm dense right adrenal nodule with
heterogeneous texture and smooth margins. Hormonal evaluation provided the following results: | |
Patient value | Reference range | | --- | --- | --- | | Serum cortisol (μg/dL)\* | 1.8 | 5.0–25.0 | | Plasma
renin activity (ng/mL per hour) | 1.10 | <0.6–4.3 | | Plasma aldosterone (ng/dL)\*\* | 6 | 3–16 | | Plasma
metanephrine (nmol/liter) | <0.2 | <0.5 | | Plasma normetanephrine (nmol/liter) | 0.6 | <0.9 | \*Cortisol
was measured at 8 a.m. following administration of 1 mg of dexamethasone at 11 p.m. the prior
evening. \*\*Aldosterone was measured with the patient in a supine position. The patient has no current
complaints, an unremarkable medical history, and a BMI of 34. Her blood pressure is 107/74 mm Hg,
and physical examination reveals no abnormalities such as striae, acne, hirsutism, bruising, fat
redistribution, or proximal muscle weakness. What is the most appropriate management for this
incidental adrenal mass? Answer Choices: (A) Repeat CT of the adrenal glands in 6 months (B)
Perform adrenal venous sampling to confirm lateralization (C) Monitor with annual biochemical testing
and imaging (D) Perform a PET scan to assess for malignancy (E) Initiate medical therapy with
spironolactone (F) Refer for a right adrenalectomy (G) Observe without intervention unless symptoms
develop (H) Perform MRI of the adrenal glands (I) Refer for partial adrenalectomy to preserve adrenal
function (J) Treat with metyrapone to suppress cortisol secretion
 A. Initiate medical therapy with spironolactone
B. Perform MRI of the adrenal glands
C. Refer for partial adrenalectomy to preserve adrenal function
D. Perform a PET scan to assess for malignancy
E. Refer for a right adrenalectomy
F. Monitor with annual biochemical testing and imaging
G. Perform adrenal venous sampling to confirm lateralization
H. Repeat CT of the adrenal glands in 6 months
I. Observe without intervention unless symptoms develop
J. Treat with metyrapone to suppress cortisol secretion
